extracted.intended_audience: responsible authorities in Kenyan public institutions (officials required to design/implement public participation), legislators, and public participation practitioners/advocates
extracted.subtask_description: A national legislative framework specifying required principles, procedures, and institutional responsibilities for designing, conducting, reporting, and evaluating public participation in Kenya. It sets general guidelines that responsible authorities must follow and flesh out in institution-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of this Act is to enhance, promote and facilitate public participation in governance processes and in particular to give effect to constitutional principles of participation; promote democracy and participation; promote transparency and accountability in decision making; enhance public awareness and understanding of governance processes; promote community ownership of public decisions; and promote public participation and collaboration in governance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the legislative aims against which public participation processes should be judged: effectiveness, promotion of constitutional participatory principles, transparency, awareness, community ownership and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to consultation and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The public, communities and organisations to be affected by a decision shall have a right to be consulted and involved in the decision making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms entitlement of affected parties to be engaged; failure to consult affected parties violates this principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of effective mechanisms for involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide effective mechanisms for the involvement of the public, communities and organizations that would be affected by or be interested in a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms must be designed to enable meaningful participation (see schedule items on notice, access, consultation framework and channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants' equitable access to the information they need to participate in a meaningful manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible authorities must ensure information is available in accessible formats, languages and through appropriate channels so all targeted participants can meaningfully engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public views in decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: Public views shall be taken into consideration in decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public input must influence decisions; authorities should document how views were considered (see 'Processing of responses' and reporting requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of appropriate feedback mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of appropriate feedback mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities should provide feedback loops so participants know outcomes and how input was used; specifics are elaborated under reporting and processing responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to national values and leadership principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to the national values under Article 10 of the Constitution and the principles of leadership and integrity set out in Chapter Six of the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation must reflect constitutional values and ethical leadership standards; conflicts with those values must be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to other prescribed principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to the principles of public participation as may be prescribed by any written law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Act works alongside other statutory requirements; responsible authorities must ensure coherence with other legal prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of sustainable decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion of sustainable decisions recognising the needs and interests of all participants, including decision makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should balance short- and long-term impacts and consider all stakeholders' interests to enhance sustainability and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of responsible authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Designates which office or body is the 'responsible authority' for developing guidelines and conducting public participation for each type of institution (e.g., parliamentary committee for Parliament, Chief Justice for Judiciary, Cabinet Secretaries for ministries, county assembly committees for county assemblies, county secretaries for county executives, and CEOs/secretaries for other public bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible authorities must develop institution-specific guidelines consistent with the general guidelines; for unspecified bodies regulations may prescribe the responsible authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of specific public participation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each responsible authority shall develop guidelines for undertaking public participation for their respective institution; those guidelines shall meet the requirements set out in the general guidelines in the Schedule and may include requirements beyond the general guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidelines must state how general requirements will be satisfied; until specific guidelines are developed, the general schedule guidelines apply as if they were the responsible authority's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of specific guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidelines developed pursuant to section 6(1) shall be published in the Gazette within three months of the commencement of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely public publication is mandated to ensure transparency and public awareness of institution-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for reasonable and meaningful public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall provide reasonable and meaningful opportunities for public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining what is reasonable consider the nature of the legislation or decision, its importance, and the intensity of its impact on the public. 'Reasonable and meaningful' implies substantive chances to influence outcomes, not merely formality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness and continuing education
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall facilitate continuing education on public engagement activities and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities should invest in capacity-building for both staff and public so engagement is informed and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider before conducting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before conducting public participation, the responsible authority shall identify the purpose of the participation; level of public participation required; urgency of the matter; number and circumstances of interested and affected parties; and the ability of targeted participants to access necessary information and the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors must inform the design of the participation exercise (scope, methods, timing, accessibility measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant institution shall give the public adequate notice to make their input on the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities must set up mechanisms to enable the widest reach—television, ICT centres, websites, community radio, public meetings, and traditional media—to ensure notice reaches intended audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and equal access to participation processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall ensure stakeholders have fair and equal access to the public participation process and the opportunity to influence the intended decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires proactive measures to remove barriers to participation and to provide equal opportunity to influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of persons with disabilities and language access
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall take all necessary measures to ensure the participation of persons with disabilities and shall provide an interpreter for participants not conversant in national languages who wish to speak in their local language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility measures (physical, sensory, communication) and language services are mandatory to achieve equitable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation framework / public participation programme requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before undertaking public participation, the responsible authority shall develop a public participation programme that clearly identifies specific purposes for consultation; the community, profession or groups to be consulted; the length of consultations; whether submissions should be oral, written or both; and the issues or matter for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes must be explicit about scope, methods, timelines and target audiences so participants understand how to engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online platform for access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall establish and ensure maintenance of an online platform to enable access, through the internet, of information relating to the institution and any other notices to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital access complements other channels; platform must be maintained and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic timeframe for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every public participation forum shall be undertaken within a realistic timeframe for consultation, allowing reasonable period for each stage of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines should be proportionate to complexity, impact and urgency; excessively short timeframes undermine meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of consultation documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation document shall be as simple and concise as possible, providing the summary of the issues or matter for consultation and clearly setting out the questions to be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, focused documents reduce barriers to engagement and improve quality of responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information — publication and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall publish and distribute documents for consideration as widely as possible (hard copies, television, advertisements, websites, community radio, traditional media) and ensure documents are in a language and form usable by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple channels and accessible formats/languages are required to reach diverse audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for information procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may request information relating to an issue under consideration; requests must be addressed to the head of the responsible authority or designated person, may be subject to reasonable fees where expense is incurred, and may be subject to confidentiality requirements. The authority may decline requests that are unreasonable or where the applicant fails to satisfy confidentiality requirements. Rights under Article 35 and freedom of information/data protection laws apply subject to this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear, fair request-handling processes and communicate any fees or confidentiality constraints; refusal must be justifiable under the stated grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of responses
rubrics_metrics.description: All responses must be carefully and independently analysed; the final decision must be made widely available to the public, including the reasons for decisions taken; and disclosure of all relevant information for the public to understand and evaluate the decision made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires documented, independent analysis and transparency about how input influenced outcomes; supports accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility, integrity and data validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities shall undertake and encourage actions that build trust and credibility; be responsible for the validity of all data collected, analyses performed, or plans developed by it or under its direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an obligation of methodological rigor, honesty in data collection/analysis, and trust-building practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonest, fraudulent or conflicted conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities and participants must not engage in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation or discrimination; must not accept payments or gifts contingent on desired results where that conflicts with professional judgment; must avoid relationships or actions that could be interpreted as conflicts of interest; and must ensure there is no misrepresentation of facts relating to the relevant body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear ethical constraints intended to preserve impartiality and public confidence; breaches may invalidate participation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant conduct standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants, including representatives of the responsible authority and respondents, shall be courteous, respectful and civil in public participation processes. Individuals who are disruptive shall be given a warning and may be removed from a meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains order and mutual respect; freedom of expression is limited to the nature and extent specified under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and publication of annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible authority shall prepare an annual report at the end of each financial year containing a description of activities and outcomes of public participation; a description of any complaints made and actions taken and the period within which complaints were addressed; and any other relevant information. The report shall be tabled (national bodies in National Assembly and Senate; county bodies in County Assembly) within three months after year end and shall be published and publicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting provides accountability and public record of participation activities, complaints handling, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cabinet Secretary may make regulations for better carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables development of further procedural/detail regulations to implement the Act; authorities must comply with regulations made under this power.
